name: 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica

leader.name: Dr. Rohit Srivastava
leader.institute: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)

organization: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)
objectives: Replacement and resupply of wintering teams at Maitri and Bharati stations.
Deployment of deep ice-core drilling equipment near Amery Ice Shelf.
Continuous atmospheric aerosol and boundary layer turbulence measurements.
Geodetic and geomagnetic baseline calibration for space weather modeling.
Environmental baseline sampling across Schirmacher Oasis and Larsemann Hills.
summary: The 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica comprised over 48 scientists, logistics specialists, and medical teams dispatched to sustain India's year-round scientific mandate across Maitri and Bharati stations, achieving crucial ice-core extractions and satellite telemetry calibrations.

timeline.title: Expedition Flag-Off from Cape Town
timeline.description: Vessel MV Vasiliy Golovnin departed Cape Town carrying scientific teams, cargo, and polar fuel.

timeline.title: Arrival at Bharati Station, Larsemann Hills
timeline.description: Ice conditions permitted safe cargo offloading; winter handover commenced for the 43rd team.

timeline.title: Transit to Maitri Station & Schirmacher Oasis
timeline.description: Helicopter sorting flights transferred equipment to the inland Schirmacher Oasis.

timeline.title: Completion of Deep Radar Sounding Campaign
timeline.description: Surveyed sub-glacial bedrock topography over 120 km of continental ice sheet traverse.

timeline.title: Return of Summer Contingent
timeline.description: Wintering-over team locked in for the polar night; summer party returned safely to Goa.

name: 42nd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
organization: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)
objectives: Installation of clean solar arrays at Bharati Station.
Comprehensive permafrost active layer monitoring in Schirmacher Oasis.
Marine ecosystem sampling along Prydz Bay.
summary: The 42nd ISEA completed critical environmental impact assessments and established automated real-time seismic monitoring nodes linked to national disaster management agencies.

timeline.title: Departure from Port Louis
timeline.description: Voyage commenced through the Roaring Forties and Furious Fifties.

timeline.title: Prydz Bay Oceanographic Casts
timeline.description: Recovered CTD casts to evaluate Antarctic Bottom Water formation.

timeline.title: Mission Conclusion
timeline.description: Summer science payloads archived and transported to NCPOR laboratories.

name: 14th Indian Arctic Expedition
organization: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)
objectives: Sustained deployment and servicing of the IndARC underwater mooring system.
Monitoring glacier retreat at Midtre Lovénbreen and Austre Brøggerbreen.
Atmospheric aerosol optical depth profiling in Kongsfjorden.
First winter Arctic research pilot phase.
summary: India's 14th Arctic Expedition marked a historic expansion with round-the-year winter presence at Himadri station in Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, focusing on the climate teleconnections between Arctic warming and the Indian summer monsoon.

timeline.title: Summer Scientific Cohort Deployment
timeline.description: First batch of scientists reached Ny-Ålesund via Longyearbyen.

timeline.title: IndARC Mooring Servicing
timeline.description: Recovered year-long deep CTD and acoustic sensor series from 192 m depth in Kongsfjorden.

timeline.title: Inaugural Winter Research Phase
timeline.description: MoES officially inaugurated year-round winter scientific operations at Himadri Station.

timeline.title: Spring Transition Phase Completed
timeline.description: Winter atmospheric and sea-ice measurements successfully transferred to NPDC servers.

name: 11th Indian Southern Ocean Expedition
organization: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)
objectives: Biogeochemical mapping across the Subtropical, Subantarctic, and Polar Fronts.
Carbon sequestration and trace metal dynamics in the Southern Ocean sink.
Deep-sea sediment coring to reconstruct paleoclimate shifts.
summary: Conducted multi-disciplinary oceanographic transects between 40°S and 67°S along the 57°30'E meridian to quantify Southern Ocean carbon cycling and primary productivity.

timeline.title: Cruise Departure from Mauritius
timeline.description: Vessel SA Agulhas steered southward crossing the Antarctic Convergence.

timeline.title: Ice-Edge Biogeochemical Stations
timeline.description: Conducted 24-hour continuous CTD profiling at the marginal ice zone.

timeline.title: Return to Port
timeline.description: Cruise terminated with over 3,200 water and sediment samples preserved.

name: Chandra Basin Glaciology Field Campaign
objectives: Annual glacier mass balance stakes measurement at Sutri Dhaka Glacier.
Ground Penetrating Radar profiling of ice thickness and subglacial bed.
Continuous hydrological runoff discharge monitoring at Chandra River gauge.
Aerosol optical depth and black carbon albedo measurements.
summary: Intensive high-altitude glaciological campaign based out of Himansh station in Lahaul-Spiti, measuring benchmark glacier retreat rates and meltwater contribution to the Indus River Basin.

timeline.title: Basecamp Re-opening at Himansh
timeline.description: Scientific team opened the high-altitude station at 4,080 m altitude.

timeline.title: Glacier Traverse & Stake Network Audit
timeline.description: Measured net annual ablation across 32 accumulation and ablation stakes.

timeline.title: Winterization and Data Uplink
timeline.description: Automated meteorological and hydrometric stations armed for automated winter recording.
